text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text: Add a single high-contrast skip link at the top of every page. It’s the fastest way to let keyboard users bypass repetitive navigation blocks and reach main content without tabbing through dozens of links. The trade-off is a tiny bit of extra layout space, but that’s negligible compared to the barrier it removes for people who rely on keyboards.

name: Reader
text: The real risk is sighted keyboard users missing the skip link entirely if it’s hidden behind a high-contrast overlay. A better alternative is a visible skip link that appears on focus, like a subtle underline or background shift, so users see it only when needed. Settle it by testing with 3 keyboard users—if they miss it, revert to a persistent visible link.

name: Ramp
text:
Add a skip link that only appears after the first tab press and hides until the next page load. It balances visibility for keyboard users with minimal visual clutter for sighted users. The trade-off is slightly more complex logic, but it keeps the interface clean while ensuring the skip link is discoverable when needed.

name: Reader
text: The real risk is sighted keyboard users never discovering the skip link if it’s hidden until the first tab press. A better alternative is a skip link that’s always visible but styled to fade into the background until focused. Settle it by testing with 3 keyboard users—if they ignore it when visible, simplify to a persistent high-contrast link.

name: Access
text: DECISION: Implement a **focus-triggered skip link**—high-contrast, full-width, visible only after first tab press, hidden until next page load. Result: Skip link exists in codebase with Playwright test coverage. Owner: accessibility-w1.
